nodes.label: Unit 5 Angles and Arcs in the circle (Geometry)
Measure arcs from central angles
nodes.description: Determine the measure of an arc as the measure of its central angle, and find the measures of adjacent arcs, semicircles and the circle by adding or subtracting.

nodes.label: Calculate arc length
nodes.description: Calculate the length of an arc as the fraction (measure of the arc / measure of the circle) of the circumference, and compare arcs of equal measure in different circles.

nodes.label: Relate arcs, chords and parallels
nodes.description: Use the corollaries on equal arcs, equal chords and parallel chords or tangents to prove arcs or chords are equal and to find unknown lengths.

nodes.label: Inscribed and central angle relation
nodes.description: Calculate the measure of an inscribed angle or of the central angle subtended by the same arc, using the theorem that the inscribed angle is half the central angle.

nodes.label: Inscribed angle and arc measure
nodes.description: Calculate an inscribed angle from its subtended arc, find arc measures from angles, and show that an angle in a semicircle is a right angle.

nodes.label: Angles from intersecting chords and rays
nodes.description: Calculate the angle formed by two chords intersecting inside a circle, or by two rays intersecting outside it, using half the sum or half the difference of the intercepted arcs.

nodes.label: Inscribed angles on the same arc
nodes.description: Find the measures of inscribed angles subtended by the same arc, and use their equality to solve for unknown angles and prove relations (e.g. equal segments).

nodes.label: Equal arcs, equal angles
nodes.description: Use equal arcs (and equal chords) in the same or congruent circles to show inscribed angles are equal, and the converse, to calculate unknowns and prove triangles isosceles.

nodes.label: Show points are concyclic
nodes.description: Decide whether four points lie on one circle by checking that two equal angles are drawn on the same base and on the same side of it.

nodes.label: Identify cyclic quadrilaterals
nodes.description: Determine whether a given quadrilateral is a cyclic quadrilateral by checking whether two angles drawn on the same base and in one direction of it are equal, and explain the answer.

nodes.label: Prove a figure is cyclic
nodes.description: Prove that a figure is a cyclic quadrilateral by showing two equal angles (such as two right angles, or angles from parallel lines) on the same base and in one direction of it.

nodes.label: Use cyclic property in deductions
nodes.description: Use a proven cyclic quadrilateral and its circle to deduce equal angles, parallel lines and the location of the centre of the circle through its vertices.

nodes.label: Opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral
nodes.description: Calculate unknown angles (and arcs) in a cyclic quadrilateral using the fact that each two opposite angles are supplementary.

nodes.label: Exterior angle of cyclic quadrilateral
nodes.description: Calculate angle measures using the corollary that the exterior angle at a vertex of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior angle at the opposite vertex.

nodes.label: Prove a quadrilateral is cyclic
nodes.description: Prove that a quadrilateral is cyclic using the converse (supplementary opposite angles) or an exterior angle equal to the interior opposite angle.

nodes.label: Tangent segments from a point outside a circle
nodes.description: Use the equality of the two tangent segments drawn to a circle from a point outside it, and the corollaries (the line through the centre and the intersection point of the tangents is the axis of the chord of tangency and bisects the angle between the tangents), to find unknown lengths and angle measures and to prove relations.

nodes.label: Circle inscribed in a polygon
nodes.description: Use the circle inscribed in a polygon (touching all of its sides internally) and equal tangent segments to find the perimeter and area of the polygon and the position of the centre.

nodes.label: Common tangents of two circles
nodes.description: Distinguish common internal and common external tangents of two circles, and solve problems finding unknown values and the length of a common tangent.

nodes.label: Calculate angles of tangency
nodes.description: Calculate the measure of an angle of tangency (or an unknown arc) using the fact that it is half the measure of the arc between its sides, and equals the inscribed angle on the same arc or half the central angle.

nodes.label: Prove cyclic quadrilaterals
nodes.description: Prove that a quadrilateral is cyclic by using the equality of the angle of tangency with the inscribed angle together with parallel lines.

nodes.label: Prove a line is tangent
nodes.description: Show that a line is a tangent to a circle by applying the converse of theorem 5 (angle with the chord equals the inscribed angle in the alternate side).
